findings.title: DMARC policy is set to 'none'

detection_methods.prior_justification: the p= tag is read directly from a record that parsed

evidence.label: TXT at _dmarc.bebeautiful.in
evidence.control_rationale: a random-label probe in the same zone; without it a wildcard would make every lookup under this domain appear to succeed

evidence.label: independent re-query via 8.8.8.8
evidence.control_rationale: the control for this re-query is the first resolver's answer, captured above

findings.description: The DMARC policy for bebeautiful.in is p=none, which asks receivers to take no action on mail that fails authentication.
findings.impact: Mail forged as this domain is still delivered. p=none is a monitoring posture, useful while you find your legitimate senders, but it stops nothing.
findings.remediation: Once your rua reports show every legitimate sender passing, change p=none to p=quarantine, then to p=reject. Move in that order and watch the reports at each step.

findings.title: No MX records published

detection_methods.prior_justification: a definite empty MX answer is a direct observation

evidence.label: MX at bebeautiful.in
evidence.control_rationale: a random-label probe in the same zone; without it a wildcard would make every lookup under this domain appear to succeed

evidence.label: independent re-query via 8.8.8.8
evidence.control_rationale: the control for this re-query is the first resolver's answer, captured above

findings.impact: Mail addressed to this domain cannot be delivered. If the domain is not meant to receive mail, saying so explicitly is better than silence.
findings.remediation: Publish MX records pointing at your mail provider. If the domain should never receive mail, publish the null MX record 'MX 0 .' (RFC 7505), which tells senders so immediately.

findings.title: No DKIM key found

detection_methods.prior_justification: the lookup produced no usable answer, so nothing moves the prior

evidence.label: TXT at sp-wildcard-probe-629fa387.bebeautiful.in
evidence.control_rationale: a random-label probe in the same zone; without it a wildcard would make every lookup under this domain appear to succeed

findings.description: None of the 17 common DKIM selectors resolved for bebeautiful.in. DKIM selector names are chosen freely by the sender and cannot be enumerated, so this does not show that the domain has no DKIM - only that we could not find a key.
findings.impact: Unknown: we could not determine whether DKIM is configured.
findings.remediation: If you know your selector, check it directly: the record lives at <selector>._domainkey.bebeautiful.in. Your mail provider's documentation names the selector it uses.

findings.title: SPF exceeds the 10 DNS lookup limit

detection_methods.prior_justification: the count is computed from records we fetched ourselves, but include chains change often and a chain we could not finish walking returns inconclusive

evidence.label: TXT at bebeautiful.in

records: v=spf1 mx a ptr include:servers.mcsv.net include:_spf.google.com include:amazonses.com include:amazonaws.com include:mail.dms.unileverservices.com -all

evidence.control_rationale: a random-label probe in the same zone; without it a wildcard would make every lookup under this domain appear to succeed

record.raw: v=spf1 mx a ptr include:servers.mcsv.net include:_spf.google.com include:amazonses.com include:amazonaws.com include:mail.dms.unileverservices.com -all
v=spf1 a mx ip4:3.212.160.81 ip4:66.189.46.252 include:_spf.google.com include:spf.protection.outlook.com ip4:20.115.101.171 -all

problems: include loop: _spf.google.com is already in the chain
include loop: amazonses.com is already in the chain

evidence.label: independent re-query via 8.8.8.8

records: v=spf1 mx a ptr include:servers.mcsv.net include:_spf.google.com include:amazonses.com include:amazonaws.com include:mail.dms.unileverservices.com -all

evidence.control_rationale: the control for this re-query is the first resolver's answer, captured above

findings.description: Evaluating this SPF policy needs 17 DNS lookups, above the limit of 10 in RFC 7208 section 4.6.4. The chain is: bebeautiful.in (8) -> servers.mcsv.net (0) -> _spf.google.com (0) -> amazonses.com (0) -> amazonaws.com (1) -> mail.dms.unileverservices.com (4) -> amazon.com (3) -> spf.protection.outlook.com (0) -> spf1.amazon.com (0) -> spf2.amazon.com (1) -> spf3.amazon.com (0).
findings.impact: Receivers stop evaluating and return permerror, so SPF fails for this domain entirely. Legitimate mail can be rejected and forged mail is not caught.
findings.remediation: Reduce the chain below ten lookups. The usual fix is to replace include: terms for providers you no longer use, and to flatten a provider's ranges into ip4:/ip6: terms - those cost no lookups at all.

findings.title: DMARC has no reporting address

detection_methods.prior_justification: the absence of a rua= tag in a parsed record is unambiguous

evidence.label: TXT at _dmarc.bebeautiful.in
evidence.control_rationale: a random-label probe in the same zone; without it a wildcard would make every lookup under this domain appear to succeed

evidence.label: independent re-query via 8.8.8.8
evidence.control_rationale: the control for this re-query is the first resolver's answer, captured above

findings.description: The DMARC record has no rua= tag, so no aggregate reports are sent anywhere.
findings.impact: Without reports there is no way to see which senders are failing authentication, which makes moving to an enforcing policy guesswork.
findings.remediation: Add 'rua=mailto:dmarc-reports@bebeautiful.in' to the record. Reports arrive daily as XML; a report analyser makes them readable.

findings.title: DMARC uses relaxed alignment

detection_methods.prior_justification: the adkim= and aspf= tags are read directly, and default to relaxed

evidence.label: TXT at _dmarc.bebeautiful.in
evidence.control_rationale: a random-label probe in the same zone; without it a wildcard would make every lookup under this domain appear to succeed

evidence.label: independent re-query via 8.8.8.8
evidence.control_rationale: the control for this re-query is the first resolver's answer, captured above

findings.description: DMARC alignment is relaxed (adkim=r, aspf=r). Relaxed alignment accepts any subdomain of bebeautiful.in in the authenticated identifier.
findings.impact: Relaxed alignment is the default and is appropriate for most senders. It does mean that anyone able to publish records under a subdomain can pass DMARC for the parent.
findings.remediation: If every legitimate sender signs and sends as the exact domain, set adkim=s and aspf=s. If subdomains send mail, relaxed is the correct setting and no change is needed.

findings.title: No MTA-STS policy published

detection_methods.prior_justification: a definite TXT answer at _mta-sts with no v=STSv1 term is direct observation

evidence.label: TXT at _mta-sts.bebeautiful.in
evidence.control_rationale: a random-label probe in the same zone; without it a wildcard would make every lookup under this domain appear to succeed

evidence.label: independent re-query via 8.8.8.8
evidence.control_rationale: the control for this re-query is the first resolver's answer, captured above

findings.description: No MTA-STS policy record is published at _mta-sts.bebeautiful.in.
findings.impact: Without MTA-STS a sending server that cannot negotiate TLS will deliver mail in plaintext rather than refusing, so an attacker positioned on the network can strip encryption and read the message.
findings.remediation: Publish a TXT record at _mta-sts.bebeautiful.in of the form 'v=STSv1; id=<timestamp>', and serve the matching policy file at https://mta-sts.bebeautiful.in/.well-known/mta-sts.txt. Start the policy in mode: testing, then move to mode: enforce.

findings.title: No SMTP TLS reporting configured

detection_methods.prior_justification: a definite TXT answer at _smtp._tls with no v=TLSRPTv1 term is direct observation

evidence.label: TXT at _smtp._tls.bebeautiful.in
evidence.control_rationale: a random-label probe in the same zone; without it a wildcard would make every lookup under this domain appear to succeed

evidence.label: independent re-query via 8.8.8.8
evidence.control_rationale: the control for this re-query is the first resolver's answer, captured above

findings.description: No SMTP TLS reporting record is published at _smtp._tls.bebeautiful.in.
findings.impact: Nobody is told when a sending server fails to establish TLS to your mail servers, so a downgrade attack or a broken certificate goes unnoticed.
findings.remediation: Publish a TXT record at _smtp._tls.bebeautiful.in of the form 'v=TLSRPTv1; rua=mailto:tls-reports@bebeautiful.in'.

findings.title: Mail can be sent as this domain

detection_methods.prior_justification: this is a simulation of a receiver's decision from records we read, not an observation of a receiver actually making it; the ratio is lower to say so

evidence.label: TXT at _dmarc.bebeautiful.in
evidence.control_rationale: a random-label probe in the same zone; without it a wildcard would make every lookup under this domain appear to succeed

evidence.label: independent re-query via 8.8.8.8
evidence.control_rationale: the control for this re-query is the first resolver's answer, captured above

findings.description: Simulating the decision a receiving mail server would make for a message forged from bebeautiful.in: it would be delivered, because the DMARC policy is p=none, which asks receivers to take no action.
findings.impact: Anyone can send mail that appears to come from this domain and expect it to reach the inbox. That is the mechanism behind invoice fraud and most credential phishing that targets a company's own staff.
findings.remediation: Publish an SPF record listing your senders and ending in -all, sign your mail with DKIM, then publish 'v=DMARC1; p=reject; rua=mailto:dmarc@bebeautiful.in' at _dmarc.bebeautiful.in. Move to p=reject only after the rua reports show every legitimate sender passing.
